scenarioStory.history: G1P0 at 40 weeks gestation with an uncomplicated, well-monitored pregnancy, presenting in active labor with contractions progressively increasing over the past 8 hours, now 2 minutes apart and lasting 60 seconds. Reports a strong urge to push and a sensation that delivery is imminent. Membranes ruptured approximately 45 minutes ago with clear fluid, no meconium.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 30-year-old G1P0 female at 40 weeks gestation with visible crowning and a strong urge to push. Contractions are 2 minutes apart and delivery appears imminent. → Controlled delivery performed: With crowning progressing, the crew supports delivery with gentle counterpressure on the head, checks for a nuchal cord, and guides delivery of the anterior and posterior shoulders before the infant delivers fully. → Newborn dried, warmed, APGAR assessed: The newborn is dried, warmed, and stimulated on the maternal chest with a strong cry and good tone. APGAR is scored at 1 and 5 minutes while the cord is clamped and cut and the placenta is allowed to deliver spontaneously.

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 30-year-old G1P0 female at 40 weeks gestation with visible crowning and a strong urge to push. Contractions are 2 minutes apart and delivery appears imminent.
relatedChecklist: Support head with gentle counterpressure to control delivery pace
Check for nuchal cord after head delivers; slip over head if present
Guide head down to deliver anterior shoulder, then up for posterior shoulder
Do not routinely suction airway during delivery, even with bulb syringe

scenarioEvents.name: Controlled delivery performed
scenarioEvents.description: With crowning progressing, the crew supports delivery with gentle counterpressure on the head, checks for a nuchal cord, and guides delivery of the anterior and posterior shoulders before the infant delivers fully.
relatedChecklist: Dry, warm, and stimulate newborn; place skin-to-skin on maternal chest
Clamp cord in two places 5-6 inches from abdomen and cut after 1-minute delay
Score APGAR at 1 and 5 minutes once neonate is stabilized
Do not pull cord; allow placenta to deliver spontaneously and contain it in a bag
Massage uterine fundus at the umbilicus to promote contraction and control bleeding

scenarioEvents.name: Newborn dried, warmed, APGAR assessed
scenarioEvents.description: The newborn is dried, warmed, and stimulated on the maternal chest with a strong cry and good tone. APGAR is scored at 1 and 5 minutes while the cord is clamped and cut and the placenta is allowed to deliver spontaneously.

scenarioEvents.name: Nuchal cord not checked before delivery
scenarioEvents.description: The crew proceeds directly to shoulder delivery without palpating for a nuchal cord. As the body delivers, the cord is found wrapped tightly around the neck, and the newborn is initially pale with a weak cry, requiring prompt cord reduction and stimulation.
relatedChecklist: Slip tight nuchal cord over shoulders instead of head; double-clamp and cut if unable
Dry, warm, stimulate newborn; position airway and reassess tone, cry, and color
